Gulab Jamun

Milk-solid dumplings fried to a deep bronze and steeped in cardamom-rose syrup until they double in size and turn to sponge. The definitive Indian celebration sweet.

★★★★★★★★★★4.7(1,688)Rated 4.7 out of 5 from 1688 reviews 45 min total Serves 8 servings Medium Indian
Jump to Recipe Jump to Method

Why This Recipe Works

Frying at a low 130°C lets the dumplings cook through to the centre before the outside sets — fried hot, they form a crust that stops syrup penetrating and leaves a raw core. The syrup must be warm rather than boiling, since hot syrup shrinks the dumplings and seals the surface.

Method

Tap a step to highlight it, or turn on Cook Mode for large type and step-by-step focus.

  1. Make the syrup first: dissolve the sugar in the water with the cardamom and saffron, bring to a boil, then simmer 5 minutes. Stir in the lemon juice and rose water and keep warm — it should be thin, not thread-forming.

  2. Mix the milk powder, flour, baking powder and salt. Rub in the melted ghee until it resembles damp sand.

  3. Add the milk a tablespoon at a time, bringing it together into a soft, slightly sticky dough. Stop as soon as it comes together — kneading makes the jamun hard.

  4. Rest, covered, for 15 minutes, then divide into 20 pieces and roll each into a perfectly smooth ball between your palms, greasing your hands lightly. Any crack will split during frying.

  5. Heat the ghee to only 130°C / 265°F — a ball dropped in should sink, then rise slowly after about 20 seconds.

  6. Fry six at a time, keeping them moving gently with a slotted spoon, for 8 to 10 minutes until evenly deep brown. Do not rush or raise the heat.

  7. Lift out, drain for 30 seconds, and slide straight into the warm syrup.

  8. Soak for at least 2 hours, turning occasionally. The jamun will swell to nearly twice their size.

  9. Serve warm or at room temperature, scattered with pistachios.

Chef’s Tips

  • Smooth, crack-free balls are essential. Roll each one for a full 20 seconds.
  • If the jamun stay hard in the centre, the dough was over-kneaded or the oil too hot.
  • A tablespoon of semolina in the dough gives a slightly firmer, more traditional bite.

Pairing Suggestions

  • Masala chai or a cold glass of milk
  • Serve after biryani or a rich curry
  • Excellent with vanilla ice cream

Storage & Reheating

Keeps 5 days refrigerated in its syrup; warm gently before serving. Freezes 2 months in syrup.
